audience.text: Java developers building server-side or desktop applications that require PDF document generation, manipulation, and conversion without third-party runtime dependencies.

capabilities.text: Create and edit PDF documents by adding pages, text fragments, tables, and annotations using Document, Page, and Paragraph APIs.
capabilities.title: PDF document creation and editing

capabilities.text: Create and manipulate AcroForm fields including text boxes, radio buttons, checkboxes, and annotations with WidgetAnnotation and RadioButtonOptionField.
capabilities.title: Interactive form field handling

capabilities.text: Encrypt and decrypt documents using AES or RC4 with StandardSecurityHandler, and sign documents with PKCS#7 via PdfSigner.
capabilities.title: Document security and encryption

capabilities.text: Convert PDF to HTML, XML, DOCX, XLSX, Markdown, or raster formats (BMP, GIF, JPEG, PNG, TIFF) and import HTML, DOCX, XLSX, or Markdown into PDF.
capabilities.title: Document conversion and export

capabilities.text: Extract and replace text using TextAbsorber and TextFragmentAbsorber, supporting right-to-left and Arabic glyph shaping.
capabilities.title: Text extraction and manipulation

capabilities.text: Split, merge, insert, extract, and reorder pages with PdfFileEditor, and render pages to raster images using device classes.
capabilities.title: Page operations and rendering

limitations.text: Concurrency: a single Document instance is not thread-safe; use one Document per thread for parallel processing.
OCR is not supported; use a dedicated OCR library for recognition of text in scanned images.
Conversion to non-PDF formats other than HTML, XML, DOCX, XLSX, and Markdown is not supported.
Full XFA form rendering is not supported; XFA data can be flattened to AcroForm but dynamic layout is not reproduced.
PdfFileSecurity.setAllowExceptions throws UnsupportedOperationException; the legacy AllowExceptions=false toolkit path is not implemented.
Text replacement with non-Latin scripts may differ from a reference renderer due to limited bidi reordering and shaping.

problems_solved.text: Enables programmatic PDF creation, editing, and conversion using a pure-Java API without external runtime dependencies.
Supports interactive form handling, annotations, and document security features for enterprise document workflows.

product_summary.text: Aspose.PDF FOSS for Java is a free, open-source, pure-Java library for creating, reading, and modifying PDF documents, targeting ISO 32000-1:2008 compliance with no third-party runtime dependencies.

workflows.name: Build and test
workflows.text: Build the project with `mvn package` and run tests with `mvn -B clean test`; CI uses Java 11 and 17 in the test matrix.

workflows.name: Install from Maven Central
workflows.text: Install the library using `mvn dependency:get -Dartifact=org.aspose:aspose-pdf-foss:26.11.0` or declare it as a Maven dependency.

workflows.name: Create and save a PDF
workflows.text: Create a new document, add a page, insert a text fragment, and save to output.pdf using the Document and Page APIs.
